The widths of the 90% confidence intervals progressively expand as the time horizon lengthens, which is a key indicator of increasing uncertainty. Conversely, substantial negative shocks—including but not limited to unforeseen economic recessions, geopolitical conflicts, significant regulatory hurdles, or company-specific operational failures like a major product recall—could cause a sharp downturn, leading to an outcome below the lower bound of the predicted range. These types of events, though less probable, inherently carry the potential to drastically alter the trajectory and lie outside the typical range of expected variability.
